article_title: Andy Burnham's push for closer EU ties causes ripples in Labour and among other parties

tasks.prompt: What central political effect of Andy Burnham's approach to Europe does the article analyse?
options: It has produced complete agreement across Labour
It has ended debate about the 2016 referendum
It concerns only technical food-export rules
It is creating divisions and strategic dilemmas within Labour and other parties
tasks.correct_answer: It is creating divisions and strategic dilemmas within Labour and other parties
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מנתחת כיצד פתיחת הדיון על קשרים קרובים יותר לאיחוד יוצרת מחלוקות בלייבור ומאתגרת גם את היריבות.

tasks.prompt: Which new agreements is Burnham expected to sign at the UK-EU summit?
options: Agreements on food, energy and youth mobility
A treaty immediately rejoining the single market
A defence pact replacing AUKUS
A customs union limited to Scotland
tasks.correct_answer: Agreements on food, energy and youth mobility
tasks.explanation_hebrew: בפסגת בריטניה–האיחוד האירופי אמורים להיחתם הסכמים בתחומי מזון, אנרגיה וניידות צעירים.

tasks.prompt: What are Labour's current manifesto red lines on the EU relationship?
options: Rejoining the EU but not its courts
No return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement
Leaving NATO and joining the euro
Following every future EU rule automatically
tasks.correct_answer: No return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement
tasks.explanation_hebrew: קווי היסוד הנוכחיים שוללים חזרה לשוק האחיד, לאיחוד המכסים ולחופש התנועה.

tasks.prompt: What does it mean that Europe is a “central plank” of Burnham's foreign policy?
options: It is a minor detail intended for one speech
It is a proposal supported only by former ministers
It is designed mainly to distract from domestic policy
It is a major supporting element of his overall policy
tasks.correct_answer: It is a major supporting element of his overall policy
tasks.explanation_hebrew: central plank הוא מרכיב יסודי ומרכזי בתוכנית או במדיניות רחבה יותר.

tasks.prompt: Why does Lord Cameron argue that talk of eventually rejoining could weaken near-term negotiations?
options: EU governments may see less reason to offer a strong partnership deal if they expect the UK to rejoin
It would prevent Burnham from travelling to Brussels
It would automatically cancel the existing trade agreement
Labour MPs would be unable to vote on food standards
tasks.correct_answer: EU governments may see less reason to offer a strong partnership deal if they expect the UK to rejoin
tasks.explanation_hebrew: קמרון טוען שאם מדינות האיחוד יחשבו שבריטניה ממילא בדרך להצטרף מחדש, יהיה להן פחות תמריץ להעניק כעת הסכם שותפות טוב.

tasks.prompt: In the article, what does a “wait and see” mindset imply among uneasy Labour MPs?
options: They have organised an immediate public rebellion
They fully support freedom of movement
They are withholding action until political consequences become clearer
They plan to leave Labour before the summit
tasks.correct_answer: They are withholding action until political consequences become clearer
tasks.explanation_hebrew: wait and see מתאר עמדה זהירה שבה ממתינים להתפתחויות, למשל לשינוי בסקרים, לפני שפועלים.

tasks.prompt: Why do attitudes to Burnham's EU strategy not divide Labour MPs along simple Leave-versus-Remain lines?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשתמש בדוגמת חבר הפרלמנט הסקוטי ולהסביר את המתח בין עמדה אישית לעקרון דמוקרטי או שיקול מחוזי.
expected_points: Some MPs who personally opposed Brexit still worry about reopening a settled referendum result
A Scottish Labour MP linked acceptance of the 2016 result to arguing that the 2014 independence vote should stand
MPs also consider constituency voting patterns, freedom of movement and electoral risk
Support or concern therefore depends on democratic and strategic arguments as well as original Brexit preference

tasks.prompt: Summarise the main supportive and cautious positions inside Burnham's cabinet.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג דמויות או טיעונים משני הצדדים ולהבחין בין הידוק קשרים לבין הצטרפות מחדש.
expected_points: Supporters argue Brexit has damaged Britain and public opinion has moved toward closer ties
Angela Rayner is described as open to changing current red lines at a future election
Shabana Mahmood stresses the costs and consequences of both rejoining and staying out
Jonathan Reynolds supports closer relations but questions customs-union or full-EU membership
Cautious figures emphasise uncertain future terms and political risk

tasks.prompt: How does Burnham's strategy create different strategic problems for the Conservatives, Liberal Democrats and Reform UK?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את האתגר הייחודי לכל אחת משלוש המפלגות, ולא רק לציין שהן חלוקות.
expected_points: Conservatives fear renewed Brexit debate could split voters, including affluent southern voters returning to the party
Liberal Democrats risk losing their distinctive position as the most pro-European large party
Reform UK sees an opportunity to unite anti-EU and Brexit-supporting voters
Burnham could simultaneously build a progressive pro-European coalition around Labour

tasks.prompt: Write a concise analysis of why reopening the Brexit debate could be both an electoral opportunity and a high-risk strategy for Labour.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לשלב טיעון להזדמנות, טיעון לסיכון וראיה פוליטית קונקרטית מן הכתבה.
expected_points: Closer ties may align Labour with public sentiment that has shifted since 2016
Economic agreements could support Burnham's claim of making people better off
The debate may consume parliamentary and government time and revive constituency divisions
Freedom of movement and referendum legitimacy could trigger internal opposition
A fall in Labour's polling lead could end the current temporary truce
